newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Tire up ahead of earnings.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Tire up ahead of earnings.

text.p: Investors flocked to Canadian Tire Corp Ltd shares on Wednesday, mirroring consumer visits to the company's stores, driving shares higher ahead of the release of the retailer's third quarter earnings tomorrow.
"Canadian Tire has demonstrated that they're one of the few retailers that could withstand the onslaught of the big boxes," said Leonard Kubas, president of Leonard Kubas consultants.
Class A shares in the automotive, leisure and home products retailer jumped 1.55 to 22.25 on nearly half a million shares today on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Vice-president of corporate affairs Alan Goddard said the Toronto-based firm will post third quarter earnings mid-day on Thursday.
Goddard said Canadian Tire and other retailers are benefitting from a moderate mood of consumer optimism for the rest of 1996 and through 1997. "I think there's a little more confidence," he said.
Kubas added that the hard goods chain has managed to hold its ground despite the entry of large-format stores such as Wal-Mart Stores Inc and Home Depot Inc.
Canadian Tire had been opening new larger stores within a short driving distance of most Canadians. "They're very well positioned," Kubas said.
The retail chain opened one of its expanded-format stores in Toronto today, Kubas said.
Kubas added that 85 percent of Canadian households shopped at Canadian Tire during the past year.

Another factor powering Canadian Tire's gains could be the resurgence of interest in retail stocks amid an extremely strong rally on the Toronto Stock Exchange, Kubas said. "A lot of retail stocks are starting to move upward."
The key 300 Composite index at Canada's largest equity exchange jumped more than 1.5 percent in late-day trading on Thursday.
